notes: Overall the architecture is well separated: services are in their own files, own their data, HTTP handling is confined to the router, and the event bus is used for cross-service events. However, main.ts directly invokes TaskService.getTask and NotificationService.createNotification in the comment.added handler, which edges into direct cross-service access rather than pure event-bus-driven communication. NotificationService is not subscribing itself; main bridges events to service methods. Completeness is strong: CRUD for users, projects, tasks, comments; member add/remove; task assign and forward-only status transitions; notifications on task.assigned, task.statusChanged, and comment.added; demo script included. Code quality issues: Router returns undefined bodies on not-found cases, can hang when required query params are missing (GET /tasks and /comments without projectId/taskId), lacks proper status codes (e.g., 400/404), minimal validation, EventBus is untyped (any). Constraints: no external dependencies, HTTP only in router, forward-only transitions, services in separate files, and exclusive data stores are satisfied; slight concern with rule 1 due to main doing cross-service reads for comment notifications.
